# Medical Machines
Well-equipped medbays have machines that diagnose, treat and even operate on patients. Each pod needs its console within a few tiles to work.
## Body Scanner
The body scanner gives a full diagnostic readout of everything wrong with a patient: fractures, internal bleeding, organ damage and more, part by part. - Put the patient in the pod, then use the console. Reading scans needs [bold]surgery training[/bold] (level 1). - [bold]Calibration[/bold]: the console can also calibrate a surgical assist. Tune each scan slice and lock the abnormal readings while the sweep is in the cyan band. You have 2 minutes, and every wrong lock costs you 8 seconds. - Succeed, and your surgery steps on that patient are [bold]twice as fast[/bold] for 10 minutes. - Fail or run out of time, and you're locked out of calibrating that patient for 10 minutes.
## Autodoc
The autodoc operates by itself, so a surgeon can queue up the work and step away. - Put the patient in the pod, then open the console. Queuing procedures needs [bold]surgery training[/bold] (level 2). - Pick a body part and the surgeries it needs, and add them to the queue. It can also run [bold]Repair Wounds / Burns[/bold] as an automated cycle. - Press [bold]Start[/bold]. The pod works through the queue on its own. It's thorough but slow: each step takes the better part of a minute. - [bold]Stop[/bold] pauses it, [bold]Clear[/bold] empties the queue, and [bold]Eject Patient[/bold] takes them out. - The pod counts as an operating table, so its steps never fail because of where the patient is lying.
## Cryo Pod
The cryo pod chills a patient down and heals them with cryoxadone. - Load a beaker of [bold]cryoxadone[/bold] into the pod, and make sure the pod is supplied with cold gas from a freezer. - Put the patient inside. Once their body temperature drops low enough, the cryoxadone slowly heals brute, burn, toxin and suffocation damage all at once. - Cryoxadone does nothing at normal body temperature. The patient has to be properly cold. - It's slow, but it needs nobody standing over it, so it's good for patients who are stable but badly hurt.
